# Upload data and prepare for plotting

CoralFuture was used to calculate EDs (ED5, ED50, ED95) using the photosynthetic efficiency data

```{r}
#  CoralFuture was used to calculate EDs: ED5, ED50, ED95 and tables are provided in Supplementary Data Sheet 1

# Upload Supplementary Excel File: Supplementary Data Sheet 1 ID25.xlsx
input_data_path <- selectFile(
  caption = "Select XLSX Input File"
)

# Porites EDs data
eds_porites  <- read_excel(input_data_path, sheet = "Data S1. Plob")
pam_porites <- read_excel(input_data_path, sheet = "Data S3. PAM Plob")

# change column names of EDs table so it fits to PAM table
eds_porites <- eds_porites %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    ED5 = "ED5 [°C]",
    ED50 = "ED50 [°C]",
    ED95 = "ED95 [°C]",
    decline_width = "Decline width [°C]",
    Genotype = "Colony no.",
    Depth = "Depth [m]"
  )

# remove the last 4 columns with the calculated mean
eds_porites <- eds_porites[, 1:(ncol(eds_porites) - 4)]

# create long format dataframe
eds_porites_long <- eds_porites %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(ED5, ED50, ED95),
               names_to = "ED_type",
               values_to = "ED_value")


# Upload Supplementary Excel File: Supplementary Data Sheet 1 ID25.xlsx
input_data_path <- selectFile(
  caption = "Select XLSX Input File"
)

# Pocillopora EDs data
eds_poc <- read_excel(input_data_path, sheet = "Data S2. Pdam")
pam_poc <- read_excel(input_data_path, sheet = "Data S4. PAM Pdam")


# change column names of EDs table so it fits to PAM table
eds_poc <- eds_poc %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    ED5 = "ED5 [°C]",
    ED50 = "ED50 [°C]",
    ED95 = "ED95 [°C]",
    decline_width = "Decline width [°C]",
    Genotype = "Colony no.",
        Depth = "Depth [m]"
  )

# remove the last 4 columns with the calculated mean
eds_poc <- eds_poc[, 1:(ncol(eds_poc) - 4)]

# create long format dataframe
eds_poc_long <- eds_poc %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(ED5, ED50, ED95),
               names_to = "ED_type",
               values_to = "ED_value")


# merge poci and porites eds data frame for plotting
eds_combined <- bind_rows(eds_porites, eds_poc)
cbass_combined <- bind_rows(pam_porites, pam_poc)
```

## Figure 2A: Photosynthetic efficiency and EDs of *Porites cf. lobata* and *Pocillopora cf. damicornis* from the shallow and deeper depth

```{r}
# Write Species name out for data anlysis and visualization
eds_combined$Species <- dplyr::recode(
  eds_combined$Species,
  "Porites cf. lobata" = "Porites lobata",
  "Pocillopora cf. damicornis" = "Pocillopora damicornis"
)
# sort coral species
eds_combined$Species <- factor(
  eds_combined$Species,
  levels = c("Porites lobata", "Pocillopora damicornis")
)

# sort reef location
eds_combined$Condition <- factor(
  eds_combined$Condition,
  levels = c("shallow", "deep")
)

# check out
# calculate mean ED5, ED50, ED95 for species and condition and create new dataframe
mean_eds_df_all <- eds_combined %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_ED5  = round(mean(ED5,  na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean_ED50 = round(mean(ED50, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean_ED95 = round(mean(ED95, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean_DW = round(mean(decline_width, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mean_eds_df_all

# Convert to long format for plotting vertical lines
mean_eds_long <- mean_eds_df_all %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_ED5, mean_ED50, mean_ED95),
    names_to = "ED_level",
    values_to = "ED"
  )

# cbass script for the PAM temperature curve with confidence interval
cbass_dataset <- preprocess_dataset(cbass_combined)
validate_cbass_dataset(cbass_dataset)

grouping_properties <- c("Condition", "Species")
drm_formula <- "Pam_value ~ Temperature"
models <- fit_drms(cbass_dataset, grouping_properties, drm_formula, is_curveid = TRUE)

eds <- get_all_eds_by_grouping_property(models)
cbass_dataset <- define_grouping_property(cbass_dataset, grouping_properties) %>%
  mutate(GroupingProperty = paste(GroupingProperty, Genotype, sep = "_"))

eds_df <- 
  left_join(eds, cbass_dataset, by = "GroupingProperty") %>%
  dplyr::select(names(eds), all_of(grouping_properties)) %>%
  distinct()


# preparation for the predict PAM values
models <- fit_drms(cbass_dataset, grouping_properties, drm_formula, is_curveid = FALSE, LL.4 = FALSE)


# The default number of values for range of temperatures is 100
temp_ranges <- define_temperature_ranges(cbass_dataset$Temperature, n=100)
predictions <- get_predicted_pam_values(models, temp_ranges)

# predictions
predictions_df <- 
  left_join(predictions,
            define_grouping_property(cbass_dataset, grouping_properties) %>% 
              dplyr::select(c(all_of(grouping_properties), GroupingProperty)),
            by = "GroupingProperty",
            relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  distinct()

#prepare summary dataframe for plotting
summary_eds_df <- eds_df %>%
 group_by(Condition, Species) %>%
    summarise(Mean_ED5 = mean(ED5),
            SD_ED5 = sd(ED5),
            SE_ED5 = sd(ED5) / sqrt(n()),
            Conf_Int_5 = qt(0.975, df = n() - 1) * SE_ED5,
            Mean_ED50 = mean(ED50),
            SD_ED50 = sd(ED50),
            SE_ED50 = sd(ED50) / sqrt(n()),
            Conf_Int_50 = qt(0.975, df = n() - 1) * SE_ED50,
            Mean_ED95 = mean(ED95),
            SD_ED95 = sd(ED95),
            SE_ED95 = sd(ED95) / sqrt(n()),
            # The value 0.975 corresponds to the upper tail probability
            # for a two-tailed t-distribution with a 95%
            Conf_Int_95 = qt(0.975, df = n() - 1) * SE_ED95) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Mean_ED50, SD_ED50, SE_ED50,
                  Mean_ED5, SD_ED5, SE_ED5,
                  Mean_ED95, SD_ED95, SE_ED95,
                  Conf_Int_5,Conf_Int_50,Conf_Int_95), ~round(., 2)))

summary_eds_df

# create result data frame
result_df <- predictions_df %>%
  left_join(summary_eds_df, by = c("Condition", "Species"))


# calculate decline width and create new dataframe
decline_width_df <- summary_eds_df %>%
  mutate(
    decline_width = Mean_ED95 - Mean_ED5
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Species, Condition, Mean_ED5, Mean_ED95, decline_width)

# prepare for plotting
decline_width_rect <- decline_width_df %>%
  mutate(
    xmin = Mean_ED5,
    xmax = Mean_ED95,
    ymin = -Inf,
    ymax = Inf
  )

# stack
decline_bar <- summary_eds_df %>%
  mutate(
    xmin = Mean_ED5,
    xmax = Mean_ED95,
    
    # stack vertically instead of overlapping
    ymin = ifelse(Condition == "shallow", 0.80, 0.83),
    ymax = ifelse(Condition == "shallow", 0.825, 0.855)
  )

# sort coral species
result_df$Species <- factor(
  result_df$Species,
  levels = c("Plob", "Pdam")
)


# CHECK OUT wihtout predictions
# visualize temperature response curve: one curve per species x depth
exploratory_curve <-
  ggplot(data = cbass_dataset,
         aes(
           x = Temperature,
           y = Pam_value,
           group = Condition,
           color = Condition)) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = drc::drm,
    method.args = list(fct = drc::LL.3()),
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Reef depth",
    values = c(shallow = "lightblue", deep = "navy")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Temperature [°C]",
    y = "Photosynthetic efficiency (Fv/Fm)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

exploratory_curve




# plot
tempresp_curve <- ggplot(
  result_df,
  aes(
    x = Temperature,
    y = PredictedPAM,
    group = GroupingProperty,
    color = Condition
  ))+
  # decline width bars
  geom_rect(
    data = decline_bar,
    aes(
      xmin = xmin,
      xmax = xmax,
      ymin = ymin,
      ymax = ymax,
      fill = Condition
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +

  # confidence interval
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = Upper,
      ymax = Lower,
      fill = Condition
    ),
    alpha = 0.2,
    color = NA
  ) +

  # fitted curve
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  # raw data
  geom_point(
    data = cbass_dataset,
    aes(
      x = Temperature,
      y = Pam_value,
      color = Condition
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +

  # ED5
  geom_vline(
    aes(
      xintercept = Mean_ED5,
      color = Condition
    ),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = Mean_ED5,
      y = 0.68,
      label = paste0("ED5")
    ),
    angle = 0,
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # ED50
  geom_vline(
    aes(
      xintercept = Mean_ED50,
      color = Condition
    ),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = Mean_ED50,
      y = 0.68,
      label = paste0("ED50")
    ),
    angle = 0,
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # ED95
  geom_vline(
    aes(
      xintercept = Mean_ED95,
      color = Condition
    ),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = Mean_ED95,
      y = 0.68,
      label = paste0("ED95")
    ),
    angle = 0,
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
facet_wrap( ~ Species,
  labeller = labeller(
    Species = c(
      Plob = "italic('Porites cf. lobata')",
      Pdam = "italic('Pocillopora cf. damicornis')"
    ),
    .default = label_parsed
  )
)+

  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Reef depth",
    values = c(
      shallow = "lightblue",
      deep = "navy"
    )
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      shallow = "lightblue",
      deep = "darkblue"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-0.02, 0.9),
    breaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.2),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
  breaks = c(28, 34, 37, 39),
  labels = c("28", "34", "37", "39")
) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Temperature [°C]",
    y = expression("Photosynthetic efficiency [Fv/Fm]")
  ) +

  theme_bw() +

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",

    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13)
  )

tempresp_curve


# save as pdf
ggsave('/pathname/Fig1A_CBASS_PAM_EDs.pdf', plot = tempresp_curve, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

```

## Figure 2B: Visual Bleaching Assessment

```{r}
# VBA data
# Upload Supplementary Excel File: Supplementary Data Sheet 1 ID25.xlsx
inout_path <- selectFile(
  caption = "Select XLSX Input File"
)

vba_data <- read_excel(input_data_path, sheet = "Data S5. VBA")

# change column names of EDs table so it fits to PAM table
vba_data <- vba_data %>%
  rename(
    VBA_1 = "VBA1 [%]",
    VBA_2 = "VBA2 [%]",
    VBA_3 = "VBA3 [%]",
    Pigmentation = "Pigmentation [%]",
    Pigmentation_retention = "Pigmentation Retention [%]")

# pigmentation retention was calculated before: (T420/T0)*100 because this describes the rention while T0-T420 is the pigmentation loss.

# Write Species name out for data anlysis and visualization
vba_data$Species <- dplyr::recode(
  vba_data$Species,
  "Plob" = "Porites cf. lobata",
  "Pdam" = "Pocillopora cf. damicornis"
)

# we are only interesting in the pigmentation retention (T0-T420) so we can remove the additional rows of T420
vba_data <- vba_data %>%
  filter(Timepoint == 0)

# make sure pigmentation is not above 100%
vba_data <- vba_data %>%
  mutate(Pigmentation_retention = ifelse(Pigmentation_retention > 100, 100, Pigmentation_retention))

# prepare for plotting
mean_pigmentation_retention <- vba_data %>%
  group_by(Species, Temperature, Condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pigmentation_retention = round(mean(Pigmentation_retention, na.rm = TRUE),0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ensure correct order of factors
vba_data <- vba_data %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = factor(Condition, levels = c("shallow", "deep")),
    Species = factor(
      Species,
      levels = c("Porites cf. lobata", "Pocillopora cf. damicornis")
    )
  )

# ensure same order in summary data: Species
mean_pigmentation_retention <- mean_pigmentation_retention %>%
  mutate(
    Species = factor(
      Species,
      levels = c("Porites cf. lobata", "Pocillopora cf. damicornis")
    )
  )
# Condition order
mean_pigmentation_retention <- mean_pigmentation_retention %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = factor(
      Condition,
  
      levels = c("shallow", "deep")
    )
  )

# plot
boxplot_pigmentation <- ggplot(vba_data,aes(x=factor(Temperature),y=Pigmentation_retention,fill=Condition))+
geom_boxplot(alpha=0.6,outlier.shape=NA,position=position_dodge(width=0.75))+
geom_point(size=0.5,alpha=0.8,aes(color=Condition),position=position_dodge(width=0.75))+
geom_text(data=mean_pigmentation_retention,aes(x=factor(Temperature),y=Inf,label=paste0(round(mean_pigmentation_retention,2)," %"),color=Condition),position=position_dodge(width=0.75),vjust=1.6,fontface="bold",size=3.3,show.legend=FALSE)+
scale_fill_manual(name="Depth location",breaks=c("shallow","deep"),values=c("shallow"="lightblue","deep"="darkblue"),labels=c("Shallow (1–3 m)","Deeper (6–12 m)"))+
scale_color_manual(breaks=c("shallow","deep"),values=c("shallow"="lightblue4","deep"="navy"))+
facet_wrap(~Species)+
scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0.05,0.25)))+
theme_bw()+
theme(legend.position="bottom",panel.grid.major=element_line(color="gray90"),panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),strip.background=element_rect(fill="white"),strip.text=element_text(face="bold"),axis.text=element_text(size=5),axis.title=element_text(size=13))+
labs(x="Temperature [°C]",y="Pigmentation retention [%]",title="Bleaching response across temperatures")

boxplot_pigmentation

#save image
ggsave('/Users/MarlenSchlotheuber/Nextcloud/10. projects/11. PhD/10. projects/Intraspecific bleaching project/Project planning/ID_2025/Data/Manuscript_Figures_Final/Suppl_Fig_VBA.pdf', plot = boxplot_pigmentation, width =8, height = 3, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

```

## Figure 2C: CBASS ED50 of *Porites cf. lobata* and *Pocillopora cf. damicornis* from the shallow and deeper depth

```{r}
# Ensure order: shallow first, then deep
# eds_combined_filtered and eds_combined
eds_combined$Condition <- factor(eds_combined$Condition,
                                     levels = c("shallow", "deep"))

# Use mean EDs for plottingen
mean_labels <- mean_eds_df_all %>%
  select(Species, Condition, mean_ED50)

# Convert to long format for plotting vertical lines
mean_eds_long <- mean_eds_df_all %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_ED5, mean_ED50, mean_ED95),
    names_to = "ED_level",
    values_to = "ED"
  )

# sort coral species
eds_combined$Species <- factor(
  eds_combined$Species,
  levels = c("Porites lobata", "Pocillopora damicornis")
)


# plot
plot_ED50 <- ggplot(eds_combined,
                          aes(x = Condition,
                              y = ED50,
                              fill = Condition)) +
  
  # Boxplot
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA) +
  
  # Raw data points
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.8,
    aes(color = Condition)
  ) +
  
  # >>> Add mean ED50 labels <<<
  geom_text(
    data = mean_labels,
    aes(
      x = Condition,
      y = mean_ED50 + 2,   # adjust upward so label sits above box
      label = paste0(" ", round(mean_ED50, 2), "°C"),
      color = Condition
    ),
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # Colors
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("shallow" = "lightblue", "deep" = "darkblue")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("shallow" = "lightblue4", "deep" = "navy")
  ) +
  
  # Facet by species
  facet_wrap(~ Species) +
  
  # Y-axis expansion
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.18))) +
  
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Reef depth",
    y = "ED50 [°C]",
    title = "ED50 differences between reef depths"
  )

plot_ED50
# figure was edited in affinity designer

# save as pdf
ggsave('/pathname/Fig1B_CBASS_ED50.pdf', plot = plot_ED50, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

```

## Figure 2D: Decline width of *Porites cf. lobata* and *Pocillopora cf. damicornis*

```{r}
# Calculate mean ED values (2 decimals)
mean_EDs <- mean_eds_df_all

# Cacluate mean decline width
decline_width_df <- mean_EDs %>%
  mutate(
    decline_width = round(mean_ED95 - mean_ED5, 2)
  ) %>%
  select(Species, Condition, decline_width)


# Mean labels for plotting
mean_labels <- decline_width_df

# decline width dots for plotting
decline_width_df <- eds_combined %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  mutate(
    decline_width  = round(ED95 - ED5, 2)
  )
    

# Plot
plot_declinewidth <- ggplot(decline_width_df,
                            aes(x = Condition,
                                y = decline_width,
                                fill = Condition)) +
  
  # Boxplot
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA) +
  
  # Raw data points
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.8,
    aes(color = Condition)
  ) +
  
  # Mean labels
  geom_text(
    data = mean_labels,
    aes(
      x = Condition,
      y = decline_width + 6,
      label = paste0(round(decline_width, 2), "°C"),
      color = Condition
    ),
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # Colors
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("shallow" = "lightblue", "deep" = "darkblue")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("shallow" = "lightblue4", "deep" = "navy")
  ) +
  
  # Facet by species
  facet_wrap(~ Species) +
  
  # Y-axis expansion
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.18))) +
  
  # Theme
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13)
  ) +
  
  # Labels
  labs(
    x = "Reef depth",
    y = "Decline Width [°C]",
    title = "Decline differences between reef depths"
  )

plot_declinewidth

# save as pdf
```

# DADA2 Pipeline: Bacterial community composition analysis

```{r}
# set working directory and upload data
cat("Reading files") # prints a message to indicate the script is starting to read files
path <- "." # current working directory
list.files(path) # lists all files in the current directory 

# Forward and reverse fastq filenames have format: 
fnFs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_R1_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_R2_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
# searches for files matching specific patterns _R1_001...and sorts files, get a sorted list of file paths for forward (fnFs) and reverse reads (fnRs)

# Extract sample names, assuming filenames have format
sample.names <- sapply(strsplit(basename(fnFs), "__|_0"), function(x) x[2])

cat("Processing",length(sample.names),"samples:", sample.names)
# outputs a summary of the number of samples detected and their names, legth(): counts the number, cat():prints the message

#Inspect read quality profiles
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[1:2])
# forwards reads
# --> Truncate the forward reads at position 280

plotQualityProfile(fnRs[1:2])
# reversed reads
# --> Truncate the forward reads at position 220 where the quality crashes

```

## Filtering and Trimming

```{r}
# filter and trimm 
cat("Filtering and trimming")

# prints a message to indicate that the filtering and triming steps are about to begin in the sequencing data processing pipeline

# Place filtered files in filtered/ subdirectory
filtFs <- file.path(path, "filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_F_filt.fastq.gz"))
filtRs <- file.path(path, "filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_R_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtFs) <- sample.names
names(filtRs) <- sample.names

### set parameters  maxN=0 (DADA2 requires no Ns), truncQ=2, rm.phix=TRUE and maxEE=2. The maxEE parameter sets the maximum number of “expected errors” allowed in a read, which is a better filter than simply averaging quality scores.
out <- filterAndTrim(fnFs, filtFs, fnRs, filtRs, truncLen=c(280,220),maxN=0, maxEE=c(2,2), truncQ=5, rm.phix=TRUE, compress=TRUE, multithread=TRUE) 

head(out)
```

## Learn Error Rate

```{r}
# learn error rates
# The error model is learned using the filtered and trimmed sequences, which helps in determining the probability of errors at each base position across the reads.Forward (errF) and reverse (errR) errors are learned separately because the forward and reverse reads often have different error profiles.

cat("Learning error rates")
errF <- learnErrors(filtFs, multithread=TRUE)
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, multithread=TRUE)

# visualize the esstimated error rates as a sanity check
plotErrors(errF, nominalQ = T)
```

## Sample interference

```{r}
# This step is essential for transforming the raw sequencing data into biologically meaningful information by correcting errors and identifying the true sequences present in your samples
# apply the core sample inference algorithm to the filtered and trimmed sequence data.
dadaFs <- dada(filtFs, err=errF, multithread=TRUE, pool = T)
dadaRs <- dada(filtRs, err=errR, multithread=TRUE, pool = T)
# It uses the error rates learned from the reverse reads (errR) to apply the error-correction model and infer the true biological sequences.

#Inspecting the returned dada-class object:
dadaFs[[1]]
dadaRs[[1]]
```

## Merging paired reads

```{r}
mergers_ID <- mergePairs(dadaFs, filtFs, dadaRs, filtRs, verbose=TRUE)
# merges forward (F) and reveres (R) sequences and filtered data in one column
# Inspect the merger data.frame from the first sample
head(mergers_ID[[1]])

# We can now construct an amplicon sequence variant table (ASV) table, a higher-resolution version of the OTU table produced by traditional methods.

seqtab_ID <- makeSequenceTable(mergers_ID)
# creates a sequence table from the merged paired-end reads. A sequence table is a matrix where: rows represent individual samples, columns represent unique DNA sequences, entries contain the counts of each sequence in each sample
dim(seqtab_ID)
# returns the dimensions of the sequence table (1st value number of rows (sample), 2nd value is the number of columns (unique sequences))

# Inspect distribution of sequence lengths
table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab_ID)))

# check visually how the districution of read length is
# Get the read length distribution
length_table_ID <- table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab_ID)))

# Convert to data frame for plotting
length_df_ID <- as.data.frame(length_table_ID)
colnames(length_df_ID) <- c("Length", "Count")

# Make sure Length is numeric
length_df_ID$Length <- as.numeric(as.character(length_df_ID$Length))

ggplot(length_df_ID, aes(x = Length, y = Count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +  # vertical bars
  labs(title = "Distribution of Read Lengths",
       x = "Read Length (bp)",
       y = "Number of Reads") +
    xlim(280, 400)+
  theme_minimal()
```

## Remove Chimerism

```{r}
# Remove chimeras  
# Chimeric sequences are artifacts of the PCR amplification process. These sequences do not represent real biological sequences but rather result from errors in the molecular processes used to prepare and sequence DNA.
# Chimeric sequences can inflate diversity estimates. Removing them ensures that the analysis focuses only on true biological sequences.
# This code removes chimeric sequences from the sequence table, calculates the dimensions of the updated sequence table and determines the proportion of non-chimeric sequences retained.

seqtab.nochim_ID <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab_ID, method="consensus", multithread=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)

dim(seqtab.nochim_ID)

## calculate the  frequency of chimeric sequences 
sum(seqtab.nochim_ID)/sum(seqtab_ID)

# Track reads through the pipeline 
# This block of code tracks the number of reads at each stage of the DADA2 pipeline for each sample. This tracking helps monitor data loss, identify problematic samples, and ensure the pipeline is functioning as expected.
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))

# custom function that calculates the total number of unique reads (amplicon sequences)
track_ID <- cbind(out, sapply(dadaFs, getN), sapply(dadaRs, getN), sapply(mergers_ID, getN), rowSums(seqtab.nochim_ID))
# combines data from multiple steps into a single table
# If processing a single sample, remove the sapply calls: e.g. replace sapply(dadaFs, getN) with getN(dadaFs)
colnames(track_ID) <- c("input", "filtered", "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nonchim")
rownames(track_ID) <- sample.names
head(track_ID)

# download table
# before downloading remove the tail of the name
track_ID_adjusted <- track_ID

rownames(track_ID_adjusted) <- rownames(track_ID_adjusted) |>
  sub("_[A-Z]\\d+_R[12]$", "", x = _) |>
  sub("^GAD_", "", x = _)

write.xlsx(track_ID_adjusted, file = "2025_ID_GAd_stats_DADA2_overview_table.xlsx", rowNames = TRUE)
```

## Assign Taxonomy

```{r}
# Assign taxonomy
# This block of code assigns taxonomic classifications to the non-chimeric sequences (ASVs) in your dataset, enabling the identification of the taxa represented by the sequences

taxa_ID <- assignTaxonomy(seqtab.nochim_ID,'/Users/MarlenSchlotheuber/Nextcloud/10. projects/11. PhD/10. projects/Intraspecific bleaching project/Project planning/ID_2025/Data/16S_Bacterial_data/16S_files/silva_nr_v138_train_set.fa.gz' , multithread=TRUE)
# uses a reference database to classify each unique sequence (ASV) in the seqtab.nochim table to a taxonomic level
# rows: correspond to unique sequences (ASV)

##optional: make species level assignments based on exact matching
taxa_ID <- addSpecies(taxa_ID, '/Users/MarlenSchlotheuber/Nextcloud/10. projects/11. PhD/10. projects/Intraspecific bleaching project/Project planning/ID_2025/Data/16S_Bacterial_data/16S_files/silva_species_assignment_v138.fa.gz')
                   
#inspect the taxonomic assignments:
taxa.print_ID <- taxa_ID # Removing sequence rownames for display only
rownames(taxa.print_ID) <- NULL
head(taxa.print_ID)
```

# **ANCOM-BC2 Analysis**

## ANCOM-BC2: Porites cf. lobata vs. Pocillopora cf. damicronis in the shallow depth

```{r}
# ANCOM try
# Make sure predictors are factors
sample_data(ps_ID_filtered)$Coral_Species <- factor(
  sample_data(ps_ID_filtered)$Coral_Species
)

sample_data(ps_ID_filtered)$Condition <- factor(
  sample_data(ps_ID_filtered)$Condition,
  levels = c("Shallow", "Deep")
)

# Check levels present in the phyloseq object
table(sample_data(ps_ID_filtered)$Coral_Species)
table(sample_data(ps_ID_filtered)$Condition)

# Check the combination of both
table(
  sample_data(ps_ID_filtered)$Coral_Species,
  sample_data(ps_ID_filtered)$Condition
)



# ANCOM-BC2
ancombc2_ID_shallow <- ancombc2(
  data = ps_ID_filtered,
  fix_formula = "Coral_Species * Condition", # the fixed factor we are interested in
  p_adj_method = "BH", # method to adjust p-value for multiple testing, by controlling FDR, Benjamini-Hochberg: common method for ASV data not too conservative and balances false positives and false ne.
  pseudo_sens = TRUE, # checks if significant taxa are sensitive to pseudo counts (diff_robust:..)
  prv_cut = 0.10, # removed very rare ASV present
  lib_cut = 100, # removes samples with low read number
  s0_perc = 0.05,  # stabilizes the test statistics by adding a small constant, default
  alpha = 0.05, # standard significance threshold
  group = NULL, # NULL because only 2 groups
  struc_zero = FALSE, # small sample size so start with False
  neg_lb = FALSE, # controls that a conservative lower bound-based approach, only used when struc_zero = T, rather for larger sample size
  pairwise = FALSE, # pairwise comparison, not used because only two groups
  global = FALSE, # only two groups
  tax_level = NULL, # ASV level wanted
  em_control = list(tol = 1e-05, max_iter = 100), # default: algorithm calcultation rounds and threshold
  verbose = TRUE # shows what is happening while the alogrith is running
)




# ANCOM-BC2
set.seed(124)

# ANCOMBC2
# first seperate phyloseq based on Coral_Species
ps_df_filtered_shallow <- subset_samples(ps_ID_filtered, Condition == "Shallow")

# check if it worked
table(sample_data(ps_df_filtered_shallow)$Condition)

# set reference level, to make sure Shallow is compared to Deep
sample_data(ps_df_filtered_shallow)$Coral_Species <- factor(
  sample_data(ps_df_filtered_shallow)$Coral_Species,
  levels = c("Por", "Poc")
)

# ANCOM-BC2
ancombc2_ID_shallow <- ancombc2(
  data = ps_df_filtered_shallow,
  fix_formula = "Coral_Species", # the fixed factor we are interested in
  p_adj_method = "BH", # method to adjust p-value for multiple testing, by controlling FDR, Benjamini-Hochberg: common method for ASV data not too conservative and balances false positives and false ne.
  pseudo_sens = TRUE, # checks if significant taxa are sensitive to pseudo counts (diff_robust:..)
  prv_cut = 0.10, # removed very rare ASV present
  lib_cut = 100, # removes samples with low read number
  s0_perc = 0.05,  # stabilizes the test statistics by adding a small constant, default
  alpha = 0.05, # standard significance threshold
  group = NULL, # NULL because only 2 groups
  struc_zero = FALSE, # small sample size so start with False
  neg_lb = FALSE, # controls that a conservative lower bound-based approach, only used when struc_zero = T, rather for larger sample size
  pairwise = FALSE, # pairwise comparison, not used because only two groups
  global = FALSE, # only two groups
  tax_level = NULL, # ASV level wanted
  em_control = list(tol = 1e-05, max_iter = 100), # default: algorithm calcultation rounds and threshold
  verbose = TRUE # shows what is happening while the alogrith is running
)


# ancom results
res_primary_ID_shallow = ancombc2_ID_shallow$res

# how many ASVs were tested in total
nrow(res_primary_ID_shallow) 
# 2655

# count how many are NA
sum(is.na(res_primary_ID_shallow$"lfc_(Intercept)"))
# 227

# find significant ASVS across Location
# counts ASVs that are significant in at least one comparison
sig_asvs_ID_shallow <- res_primary_ID_shallow[res_primary_ID_shallow$diff_Coral_SpeciesPor == TRUE, ]

# how many remain
nrow(sig_asvs_ID_shallow)
# 939

# counts ASVs that are significant in at least one comparison
sig_asvs_ID_shallow <- sig_asvs_ID_shallow[sig_asvs_ID_shallow$passed_ss_Coral_SpeciesPor == TRUE, ]

nrow(sig_asvs_ID_shallow)
# 155 sig ASV passed the ANCOM-BC2 sensitivity analysis = result is robust

# download sig ASV ANCOM-BC2 table
write.xlsx(sig_asvs_ID_shallow, file = "/Users/MarlenSchlotheuber/Nextcloud/10. projects/11. PhD/10. projects/Intraspecific bleaching project/Project planning/ID_2025/Data/16S_Bacterial_data/ANCOM/2025_ID_GAd_sig_asv_ANCOMBC2_PorvsPoc_shallow.xlsx", rowNames = TRUE)


# extract taxonomy from phyloseq
tax_ID <- tax_table(ps_ID_filtered)
tax_ID_df <- as.data.frame(tax_ID)
tax_ID_df$taxon <- rownames(tax_ID_df)

# join taxonomy
sig_asvs_tax_ID_shallow <- sig_asvs_ID_shallow %>%
  left_join(
    tax_ID_df %>% select(taxon, Phylum, Order, Family, Genus, Species),
    by = "taxon"
  )

# replace missing Family names
sig_asvs_tax_ID_shallow <- sig_asvs_tax_ID_shallow %>%
  mutate(Family = ifelse(is.na(Family), "Unknown", Family))

# create combined ASV-family label
sig_asvs_tax_ID_shallow <- sig_asvs_tax_ID_shallow %>%
  mutate(ASV_Family = paste(taxon, Family, sep = "_"))

# keep only the log fold change column for Top vs Bottom
heatmap_df_ID_shallow <- sig_asvs_tax_ID_shallow %>%
  dplyr::select(ASV_Family, lfc_Coral_SpeciesPoc) %>%

)
```

```{r}
  data = ps_df_filtered_deep,

  p_adj_method = "BH", # method to adjust p-value for multiple testing, by controlling FDR, Benjamini-Hochberg: common method for ASV data not too conservative and balances false positives and false ne.
  pseudo_sens = TRUE, # checks if significant taxa are sensitive to pseudo counts (diff_robust:..)
```

# Supplementary Tables

## Remove Outliers

```{r}
# the IQR method
# What is Interquartile ranges or IQR?
# The IQR describes the middle 50% of values when ordered from lowest to highest.
# The IQR is then the difference between Third quartile and First quartile.
# General equation to calculate Interquartile range or in other words the bulk of values. To determine IQR we need to get Third quartile and first quartile.

# What is Quartiles?
# Likewise percentile, a quartile instead cuts the data in 4 equal parts. Hence, 25th percentile is our first quartile, 50th percentile is second quartile, 75th percentile is our third quartile.
# --> Then use IQR to calculate the limits for our values to lie in between.

# Write Species more simple for data anlysis and visualization
eds_combined$Species <- dplyr::recode(
  eds_combined$Species,
  "Porites cf. lobata" = "Porites lobata",
  "Pocillopora cf. damicornis" = "Pocillopora damicornis"
)

# create three new dataframes for ED5, ED50 and ED95
eds_ED5 <- eds_combined %>%
  select(-ED50, -ED95)

eds_ED50 <- eds_combined %>%
  select(-ED5, -ED95)

eds_ED95 <- eds_combined %>%
  select(-ED5, -ED50)

# Identify outliers in ED5 by Species and Condition
eds_ED5_clean <- eds_ED5 %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>% # group by Species and Condition to detect outliers
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(ED5, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),   # determines the firt quantile: the 25% quantile of ED5
    Q3 = quantile(ED5, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),   # determines the third quantil the 75% quantil of ED5
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,                            # determines the middle 50% of values, difference between third and first                                                 quartile
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR,                   # defines the lower outlier boundary, 1.5 is defined by the Tukey method
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR,                   # defines the upper outlier boundary
    is_outlier = ED5 < lower | ED5 > upper    # define outliers when they are lower or higher than the range
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# check outliers
eds_ED5_clean %>% filter(is_outlier == TRUE)

# remove outliers
eds_ED5_nooutliers <- eds_ED5_clean %>% 
  filter(is_outlier == FALSE)

# check sample number before and after removing outliers 
eds_ED5 %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
# Porites: 20,20 Poci: 25, 25

eds_ED5_nooutliers %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
# Porites: 17, 18, Poci: 24, 24

# inspect visually
ggplot(eds_ED5_clean, aes(x = Condition, y = ED5, color = is_outlier)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~Species)


# Identify outliers in ED50 by Species and Condition
eds_ED50_clean <- eds_ED50 %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(ED50, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), # extract 25th percentile
    Q3 = quantile(ED50, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), # extract 75 percentile
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR,  # calculate lower and upper bounds
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR,
    is_outlier = ED50 < lower | ED50 > upper
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# check outliers
eds_ED50_clean %>% filter(is_outlier == TRUE)

# remove outliers
eds_ED50_nooutliers <- eds_ED50_clean %>% 
  filter(is_outlier == FALSE)

# check sample number before and after removing outliers 
eds_ED50 %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
# Porites: 20,20 Poci: 25, 25

eds_ED50_nooutliers %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
# Porites: 16, 18 Poci: 25, 24

# Identify outliers in ED95 by Species and Condition
eds_ED95_clean <- eds_ED95 %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(ED95, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(ED95, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR,
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR,
    is_outlier = ED95 < lower | ED95 > upper
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# check outliers
eds_ED95_clean %>% filter(is_outlier == TRUE)

# remove outliers
eds_ED95_nooutliers <- eds_ED95_clean %>% 
  filter(is_outlier == FALSE)

# check sample number before and after removing outliers 
eds_ED95 %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
# Porites: 20,20 Poci: 25, 25

eds_ED95_nooutliers %>%
  group_by(Species, Condition) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
# Porites: 19,17 Poci: 24,24

# create new dataframe without outliers
eds_nooutliers_long <- bind_rows(
  eds_ED5_nooutliers  %>% mutate(ED_type = "ED5",  ED_value = ED5),
  eds_ED50_nooutliers %>% mutate(ED_type = "ED50", ED_value = ED50),
  eds_ED95_nooutliers %>% mutate(ED_type = "ED95", ED_value = ED95)
) %>%
  select(-ED5, -ED50, -ED95)

#check data frame
eds_nooutliers_long %>%
group_by(Species, Condition, ED_type) %>%
summarise(n = n())

```

# Statistical analysis

## Thermal response - depth differences

```{r}
# Thermal tolernace: ED50

# check assumptions
# Is data normally distributed
hist(eds_combined$ED50) # right skewed

# run linear model first for inspecting the data and model assumptions
model_ED50 <- lm(
  ED50 ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_combined
)

summary(model_ED50)
anova(model_ED50)

# check residuals
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_ED50)

# insprect normality
shapiro.test(residuals(model_ED50))
# significant, not normally distirbuted

#inspect homogeneity of variance
leveneTest(
  ED50 ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_combined
)
# significant --> do robustness check for significant results

# permutation two-way anova
set.seed(123)

perm_ED50 <- aovperm(
  ED50 ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_combined,
  np = 9999,
  method = "freedman_lane"
)

perm_ED50

# sensitivity check because levene test is significant
model_ED50 <- lm(
  ED50 ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_combined,
  contrasts = list(
    Species = contr.sum,
    Condition = contr.sum
  )
)

Anova(model_ED50, type = 3, white.adjust = "hc3")
# same result as the ANOVA: results are robust.

# Is data normally distributed
hist(eds_combined$ED5)
```

```{r}
p_raw_condition

p.adjust(p_raw_condition, method = "holm")
# in both species signficiant

# Supplementary Table S8
# Species effect within shallow
set.seed(123)
shallow_test <- independence_test(
  ED50 ~ Species,
  data = subset(eds_combined, Condition == "shallow"),
  distribution = approximate(nresample = 9999)
)

# Species effect within deep
set.seed(123)
deep_test <- independence_test(
  ED50 ~ Species,
  data = subset(eds_combined, Condition == "deep"),
  distribution = approximate(nresample = 9999)
)

p_raw_species <- c(
Shallow = pvalue(shallow_test),
  Deep = pvalue(deep_test)
)

p_raw_species
# shallow; significant
# deep: not significant

# Holm correction
p.adjust(p_raw_species, method = "holm")



# Supplementary Table S9
# Thermal limit: ED95
# run linear model first for inspecting the data and model assumptions
model_ED95 <- lm(
  ED95 ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_nooutliers
)

summary(model_ED95)
anova(model_ED95)

# check residuals
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_ED95)

# insprect normality
shapiro.test(residuals(model_ED95))
# not significant

#inspect homogeneity of variance
leveneTest(
  ED95 ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_nooutliers
)
# significant

# permutation two-way anova
set.seed(123)

# Two-way ANOVA
model_ED95 <- aov(
  ED95 ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_nooutliers
)

# ANOVA table
summary(model_ED95)
# not significant


# Supplementary Table S10
# Decline width

# prepare data
# seperate data by species
eds_porites_filtered <- subset(eds_combined, Species == "Porites cf. lobata")
eds_poci_filtered    <- subset(eds_combined, Species == "Pocillopora cf. damicornis")

# remove outliers of DW for porites
# Without Outliers
# Identify outliers in ED5 by Condition
eds_porites_filtered_clean <- eds_porites_filtered %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>% 
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(decline_width, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),  
    Q3 = quantile(decline_width, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),  
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,                            
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR,                   
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR,                   
    is_outlier = decline_width < lower | decline_width > upper    
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# check outliers
eds_porites_filtered_clean %>% filter(is_outlier == TRUE)

# remove outliers
eds_porites_nooutliers <- eds_porites_filtered_clean %>% 
  filter(is_outlier == FALSE)

# check sample number before and after removing outliers 
eds_porites_nooutliers %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
# 19, 18

# remove outliers of DW for poci
# Identify outliers in ED5 by Condition
eds_poci_filtered_clean <- eds_poci_filtered %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>% 
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(decline_width, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),  
    Q3 = quantile(decline_width, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),  
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,                            
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR,                   
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR,                   
    is_outlier = decline_width < lower | decline_width > upper   
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# check outliers
eds_poci_filtered_clean %>% filter(is_outlier == TRUE)

# remove outliers
eds_poci_nooutliers <- eds_poci_filtered_clean %>% 
  filter(is_outlier == FALSE)


# combine dataframes
eds_combined_nooutliers <- bind_rows(eds_porites_nooutliers, eds_poci_nooutliers)

# SUpplementary Table S10
# 1. CHECK ASSUMPTIONS
model_DW <- lm(
  decline_width ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_combined_nooutliers
)

summary(model_DW)
anova(model_DW)

# check residuals
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_DW)

# insprect normality
shapiro.test(residuals(model_DW))
# significant

#inspect homogeneity of variance
leveneTest(
  decline_width ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_combined_nooutliers
)
# significant

# permutation two-way anova
set.seed(123)

perm_DW <- aovperm(
  decline_width ~ Species * Condition,
  data = eds_combined_nooutliers,
  np = 9999,
  method = "freedman_lane"
)

perm_DW
```

## PCoA Plot ITS2

```{r}
# all data: bray_its2, metadata_its2
# porites: bray_porites, metadata_its2_porites
# Pocillopora:  bray_pocillopora, metadata_its2_pocilloproa

# sqrt data
its2_bray_sqrt <- sqrt(bray_its2)

# PCoA
its2_pcoa <- cmdscale(
  its2_bray_sqrt,
  k = 2,
  eig = TRUE,
  add = TRUE
)

# Calculate variance explained
its2_eig <- its2_pcoa$eig

PCoA1_var <- round(
  100 * its2_eig[1] / sum(its2_eig[its2_eig > 0]),
  1
)

PCoA2_var <- round(
  100 * its2_eig[2] / sum(its2_eig[its2_eig > 0]),
  1
)

# Create PCoA dataframe
its2_pcoa_df <- data.frame(
  sample_name = rownames(its2_pcoa$points),
  PCoA1 = its2_pcoa$points[, 1],
  PCoA2 = its2_pcoa$points[, 2]
)

# Add metadata
its2_pcoa_df <- its2_pcoa_df %>%
  left_join(
    metadata_its2,
    by = "sample_name"
  )

# Plot
pcoa_its2_host <- ggplot(
  its2_pcoa_df,
  aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = Species)
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  stat_ellipse(
    aes(group = Species),
    type = "norm",
    level = 0.95,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Condition) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PCoA1 (", PCoA1_var, "%)"),
    y = paste0("PCoA2 (", PCoA2_var, "%)"),
    color = "Coral Species"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

pcoa_its2_host

# save
ggsave("/Users/MarlenSchlotheuber/Nextcloud/10. projects/11. PhD/10. projects/Intraspecific bleaching project/Project planning/ID_2025/Data/Suppl_Figures/PCoA_Poc_Por_ITS2.jpg", plot = pcoa_its2_host, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300)

ggsave("/Users/MarlenSchlotheuber/Nextcloud/10. projects/11. PhD/10. projects/Intraspecific bleaching project/Project planning/ID_2025/Data/Suppl_Figures/PCoA_Poc_Por_ITS2.pdf", plot = pcoa_its2_host, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# Plot
pcoa_its2_depth <- ggplot(
  its2_pcoa_df,
  aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = Condition)
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  stat_ellipse(
    aes(group = Condition),
    type = "norm",
    level = 0.95,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "shallow" = "lightblue",
      "deep" = "darkblue"
    )
  ) +

    x = paste0("PCoA1 (", PCoA1_var, "%)"),
    y = paste0("PCoA2 (", PCoA2_var, "%)"),
    color = "Depth Location"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

pcoa_its2_depth

# save
```
